newsitem.title: UK: UK's Heseltine won't contest party leadership.
newsitem.headline: UK's Heseltine won't contest party leadership.

text.p: Former British deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine said on Saturday he would not be a candidate for the leadership of the defeated Conservative Party after John Major stood down as leader.
Conservative Central Office said Heseltine, 64, had been taken to hospital after suffering "mild agina pains" but had not had a heart attack.

"He would like to confirm that he will not be a candidate in the leadership campaign for the Conservative Party," Conservative Central Office said in a statement. Heseltine had been considered one of the front-runners to replace Major after Thursday's crushing election defeat.
The Conservatives said Heseltine was having tests in hospital. "He has not had a heart attack and hopes to be home in a few days," Central Office said.
Four years ago, Heseltine suffered a heart attack while on holiday in Venice.
So far, only former chancellor (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke has stepped forward as a candidate for the party's leadership.
